# arch_baseline.txt -- the architecture ratchet: findings of zl lint --full --arch per
# (rule, file). A count may only go DOWN; lower a row as the findings are fixed, delete
# it at zero. The target for every row is zero. ztestrunner's arch kind enforces it.
#
# FIRST SANCTIONED EXCEPTION, A001 and A003 src/ztypes.z: isCReserved names the C
# reserved words and the numeric-suffix table names zerolang's width suffixes, and both
# compare a spelling because the spelling IS the datum -- there is no id to compare a C
# keyword against. All 54 A001 findings in the file are those two tables (38 and 16), and
# the row rises only when C gains a word the emitter must dodge, with the word named in
# the commit message. Every other row still only goes down.
#
# SECOND SANCTIONED EXCEPTION, A001 src/zl.z: the flag and subcommand chain compares argv
# text. A command-line flag has no id to compare against -- the spelling IS the datum,
# for the same reason ztypes.z's C-keyword table is sanctioned above -- and all 23 A001
# findings in the file are that one chain. The row rises by exactly one per flag or
# subcommand added, with the flag named in the commit message. Every other row still
# only goes down.
#
# THIRD SANCTIONED EXCEPTION, A001 lib/system/zlexer.z: kwlookup and
# islookupReserved are the keyword and reserved-word tables. A keyword has no id to
# compare against -- the spelling IS the datum, the same reasoning as ztypes.z's
# C-keyword table and zl.z's flag chain above -- and all 40 A001 findings in the file
# are those two tables, 0 elsewhere. The row rises by exactly one per keyword or
# reserved word added, with the word named in the commit message. Every other row
# still only goes down.
